extraction.policy_amends: P05 section 5's refusal of linked entries, for this archive only
steps: archive SHA-256 equals the pin before any member is read
every member name relative and normalized; an absolute, traversing or duplicate name refuses the whole archive
an independent author freezes the complete member inventory (name, type, size, mode, link target) at preparation, before extraction

extraction.receipt_rule: _check_installation's selected-Node receipt adapts to this layout under the 0.2.0 schemas
extraction.provenance_writer: the preparer writes NODE-SOURCE.json at MP (not taken from the archive); its exact bytes are frozen in the reviewed preparation plan before publication; the exact-tree check and no-replace publication cover it as a planned non-archive file; MP's independent reviewer checks it; the provider reads it at preflight

node.executable_pin: SHA-256, size and mode recorded at preparation and frozen in the reviewed execution plan before any start
node.destination: an absent task-specific directory; never replaces another executable

python.interpreter: the C271 worktree's own .venv, created in place from main's committed local environment specification
python.observed_today: CPython 3.12.13 (Homebrew); the venv's python3.12 is the framework launcher (about 52 KB), which re-executes Resources/Python.app/Contents/MacOS/Python; the interpreter code is in the framework's Python library
bound_by_m0: installation-tree inventory by path and SHA-256, symlinks by target, of every regular file of the framework version directory .../Python.framework/Versions/3.12/: Resources/Python.app/Contents/MacOS/Python (the process image), the Python library, bin/python3.12, the standard library with its __pycache__ bytecode, lib-dynload
every file of the .venv, including pyvenv.cfg and site-packages, with the seven packages' RECORD files verified
every Mach-O dependency outside /usr/lib/ and /System/Library/ of every Mach-O file in those trees (for example Homebrew's OpenSSL)
python.claim: binds the files of the interpreter installation and the non-system libraries its Mach-O files reference; not their runtime behaviour, nor files that libraries load at run time by their own logic (for example OpenSSL's configuration and provider modules); weaker than E4's single image pin

mach_o_rules.rpath: every LC_RPATH entry recorded; an @-relative LC_RPATH entry (for example libmpdec's @loader_path/../lib) is a search directory, resolved as a directory; a reference found through it must still resolve to a bound file
mach_o_rules.at_references: accepted only if, by dyld's rules with the recorded rpaths, the reference resolves to a bound file

python.exact_sets: both trees compared as exact sets at every check; an extra, missing or changed file refuses; bytecode files belong to the set and an added __pycache__ file refuses
python.dependencies: bound transitively by each referenced path, with every symbolic-link hop recorded (for example <prefix>/opt/openssl@3 to its Cellar directory) and followed again at each check
python.interpreter_selection: the chain from .venv/bin/python to python3.12, through the <prefix>/opt/python@3.12/... links, and pyvenv.cfg's home are bound; the resolved launcher path is checked again at each use

dependencies.kinds: JavaScript, JSON or text; no native module

supervisor.reimplemented: run_process, with the original signature and receipt fields
supervisor.only_change: the Linux precondition prctl(PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER) is replaced by: sys.platform == 'darwin', machine arm64, sysctl.proc_translated == 0 (sysctlbyname); failure raises the same kind of Stop
supervisor.original_supervisor: byte-identical; stays the Linux contract's supervisor

kept: one direct child in its own session and process group
bounded capture, deadlines, no retry, receipts, handles closed
a live member of the child's process group after exit refuses the run
SIGTERM then SIGKILL of the group within 2,000 ms
not_kept: orphaned descendants re-parented to the supervisor (Darwin re-parents them to launchd)
guarantees.source_backed_property: to be shown by the reviewed static check MC11 (NOT_RUN): the probe, module loader and 24 reader files make no use of child_process, cluster, worker_threads or process.dlopen

assertion_meanings.reaped: the direct child was reaped; orphaned descendants are re-parented to launchd, not to the supervisor
assertion_meanings.process_group_absent: killpg(pid, 0) finds no member of the child's group; whether Darwin counts a zombie member is not established
assertion_meanings.cleanup.passed: the group was gone within the cleanup ceiling, with the two meanings above

supervisor.durability: the probe's fs.fsyncSync is unchanged; on macOS fsync does not force data to permanent storage as F_FULLFSYNC does; results claim no durability beyond fsync

static_scan.rule: every dynamic construct found is reviewed
static_scan.limit: a scan of names cannot exclude every dynamic route; the result states that limit

preparer.rules: P05 section 5, amended for the official archive's member policy (section 3) and the planned non-archive NODE-SOURCE.json
preparer.publication: renamex_np(staged, destination, RENAME_EXCL) from libSystem within one volume; ENOTSUP or any failure refuses; never a fallback rename
preparer.flag_binding: the implementation binds RENAME_EXCL's value from the SDK header or Apple's documentation and proves no-replace with control MC15

fields: product version, build, ProductVersionExtra, and the OS cryptex's SystemVersion.plist if present
Git implementation used for source reads: absolute path (not the /usr/bin/git dispatcher), SHA-256, version from one bounded --version start
exact declared environment plus __CF_USER_TEXT_ENCODING with its recorded value when CoreFoundation added it (S10)

host_observation.closure_claim: The Node executable's bytes and load commands are bound, and so is the interpreter installation of section 4 within the limits stated there; the system libraries come from the OS build's dyld shared cache in the signed system volume and the OS cryptex and are identified only by the recorded OS product version, build and cryptex version, not by per-file hashes; Apple's sealed system volume and SIP are assumed, not verified.
canonical_paths: every bound path recorded canonically (realpath once, rechecked before use)
/tmp, /var and /etc resolve into /private; any other symlinked ancestor refuses
qualifying runs use a resolved temporary directory
a .DS_Store or other untracked file in a source, evidence or dependency tree refuses it
host_observation.boot_binding: the provider reads kern.bootsessionuuid before the cohort and before and after each start; a change fails the attempt; the probe checks os.type(), os.release(), os.machine() and the OS build file, and no longer checks the boot itself (stated weakening of E19)
host_observation.N34_M: before a macOS execution plan is adopted, an independent reviewer examines the Mach-O parser's source and the closure claim against the actual load commands; an external review obligation, not a runtime pass
host_observation.execution_plan_rules: P07 section 2 (E9, E17): literal argv with cwd, environment and limits; canonical paths; no TODO, null, wildcard, guessed hash or unresolved field; existing external evidence parent with ancestor identities; absent per-attempt output paths; approved failure capture; independent review with an externally supplied digest

selection_rule.qualifying_run: driver receives --readback-config and --readback-config-sha256 from an independently reviewed execution plan; all existing rules apply; any skip, error, expected failure or missing method of the readback cohort fails the run; only a qualifying run can be cited for the readback methods, the macOS qualification or R03
selection_rule.ordinary_run: neither argument: the driver proceeds with every stage, records readback_selection {status: absent, run_kind: ordinary} and passes no selection to the unit process; the readback CPU class's setUpClass fails visibly with 'No approved current-host readback selection: ordinary run, not a qualification'; unittest reports one class-level error and neither runs nor reports the class's three methods; never a skip; coordinator seams run; the unit stage is failed for this reason under both drivers' rule that any skip, error or failure fails a stage; no ordinary run is evidence for the readback methods
selection_rule.partial_selection: fails in either kind of run
selection_rule.direct_invocation: without the driver: an ordinary run (visible setup error) unless both selection variables are set, as P05 section 2 provides
selection_rule.amends: only the driver's refusal to start without a selection, for ordinary runs; P05's no-skip rule and CH13's 'fails visibly; no skip' stay
rejected_alternatives: revision 1's labelled skip for ordinary runs: adds a skip, which P05 forbids, and changes no stage outcome under the drivers' zero-skip rule
requiring a selection for every run: main's ordinary routine would run no stage without one
selection_rule.today: the branch's driver refuses to start any step without a selection; main's driver has no readback selection and main's version of the test skips the three CPU methods
selection_rule.r04_obligation: after integration, main's ordinary runs would change from three skipped methods to one class-level setUpClass error with the three methods not executed (tests run -3, skipped -3, errors +1); R04 classifies this change under OK-ENG-009 section 3, items 2 and 4, with exact inputs, and states whether the readback methods belong to released behaviour; this contract does not decide it
